description: This bar chart, from the paper “WebGLM: Towards An Efficient Web-Enhanced Question Answering System with Human Preferences,” illustrates the time in seconds required for three distinct stages—Search, Extract, and Retrieval—for four different performance levels: Average, 50%, 75%, and 90%. The horizontal axis displays these four performance levels in ascending order from left to right. The vertical axis, labeled “sec.” for seconds, is scaled linearly from 0.0 to 8.0, with tick marks at every 2.0 unit interval. Each bar is a stacked composition, with the bottom segment representing “Search” (dark blue), the middle segment representing “Extract” (medium blue), and the top segment representing “Retrieval” (light blue). The “Search” stage consistently consumes the least time, with values approximately 1.0–1.5 seconds across all performance levels. The “Extract” stage is the largest contributor to the total time, ranging from approximately 2.0 to 3.0 seconds. The “Retrieval” stage is the smallest component, typically around 0.5–1.0 seconds. The total time for each performance level increases from left to right, with the 90% level showing the highest cumulative time, reaching approximately 7.0 seconds, while the Average level is lowest at approximately 4.5 seconds. The bars are not sorted; they are presented in the order of performance level from left to right. No bars are visually emphasized or annotated beyond their standard color-coded segments.
